data.why: The demo bundles a matched, anonymized IHC Excel (Patwin) and MammaTyper PDF pair, with one intentional discordance, that the app's own cover page offers for download and that Paso 1's uploaders expect; these are the only files the pipeline can fuse by sample_id.

goals: Upload the matched IHC Excel and MammaTyper PDF and run the fusion pipeline to cross-match samples by sample_id
Classify each sample into a St. Gallen molecular subtype (Luminal A, Luminal B HER2+/-, HER2-enriched, Triple negative) from the fused biomarker values
Review per-biomarker concordance statistics (Cohen's kappa, McNemar test, sensitivity/specificity, PPV/NPV, diagnostic OR) between IHC and RT-qPCR
Identify and investigate the automatically flagged clinical alerts (discordances, HER2-low without documented score, values near cut-off)
Export a per-sample PDF report and a batch Excel report (technical table + concordance dashboard)
Browse the cumulative historical database and global statistics across processed batches

review.summary: The tree follows the whole MammaScope flow faithfully: upload, fuse by sample_id, alerts, the concordance heatmap, exports, the global statistics module, SQL history and thresholds. Every one of the 13 screens I opened supports its node. It needs a small fix before filing: the St. Gallen subtype comparison, which is central to the README, is underplayed, and a few UI-noise actions and the feature-to-task links need tidying.
